Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of presentation: Adult patient with acute central chest pressure described as “sitting on my chest,” with shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea, left arm pain, calf pain and leg swelling, and reduced exertional tolerance. Risk factors include hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and current smoking. Ambulance requested; pre-hospital evaluation planned; evaluation by hospital clinician indicated.
- Relevant differential diagnoses ( aligned with transcript and DDx, with likelihood):
  - Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina / NSTEMI) — High
    - Rationale: Central chest pressure with exertional onset, left arm radiation, dyspnea, nausea, and multiple cardiovascular risk factors.
  - Pulmonary embolism (with possible DVT) — Medium
    - Rationale: Acute chest symptoms with dyspnea and leg symptoms (calf pain, swelling); sudden onset during activity.
  - Musculoskeletal chest wall pain (costochondral strain) — Medium
    - Rationale: Onset during gardening; chest-wall location and pressure quality; activity-related.
- Note on contradictions: Not recorded in transcript vs. DDx; no conflicts noted.
- Plan synthesis: High concern for cardiac etiology; arrange urgent hospital evaluation via ambulance; paramedics to monitor and assess blood pressure, heart rate, and breathing; provide patient with instructions and involve spouse to gather belongings; hospital consultation anticipated on arrival.
- Management Plan (management_plan_main_or_not_recorded): Ambulance transport to hospital for urgent cardiopulmonary evaluation; maintain calm, provide water if needed, do not take additional medications; paramedics to assess vitals and monitor; hospital consultant to evaluate for ACS and related conditions.
